iOS 26.6 is set to roll out to iPhone users next week, and Apple's release notes have made it clear what to expect from this software update.

iOS 26.6 brings Spotlight optimisations ahead of the iOS 27 upgrade, along with security patches and bug fixes.

Earlier this week, Apple seeded the RC (Release Candidate) build of iOS 26.6 to developers and public beta testers. That means the official public release is just around the corner.

iOS 26.6 is expected to launch officially early next week, alongside companion updates such as macOS Tahoe 26.6. The earliest possible arrival date is Monday, July 27.

These new updates aren't focused on adding new features, but rather on making iOS 26 more stable, secure, and less buggy, while also preparing your iPhone for the upgrade to iOS 27.

Here's what Apple's official release notes say:

Apple will reveal the specific security update contents when the software officially rolls out next week. But the most notable detail involves Spotlight indexing.

iOS 27 is coming this fall with a complete overhaul of the Spotlight search function. To prepare for this change, iOS 26.6 will begin the work of optimising iPhone Spotlight indexing early.

When the first iOS 27 developer beta dropped, testers discovered that the Spotlight indexing process could take a long time — up to a week or more. By starting that process early in iOS 26.6, users will enjoy a smoother first-time experience when iOS 27 officially launches.

Beyond those changes, iOS 26.6 also adds a notification when you've hit the limit for blocked contacts, and includes a new anti-theft feature code, though that functionality may not arrive until later.

How is iOS 26 running on your device? Are there any bugs you're still hoping Apple will fix soon? Drop us a line in the comments.
